scope: schema: packages/db/prisma/schema/*.prisma — 196 models gain a `/// @dpf` documentation line (lifecycle class, retention disposition, sensitivity, categories, regulated scope, owner, steward, time axis); no column, type, index, relation, enum or migration changes; lifecycle: scripts/portal-migrate-boot.sh runs packages/db/scripts/apply-model-metadata-comments.ts (COMMENT ON TABLE only)
rationale: EP-A33A5C61 slice 4 (BI-D9F158AF), founder direction 2026-09-08: declare governance metadata once, on the model, and carry it in the Postgres catalog instead of in four parallel TypeScript homes (table-classification.ts, the govern/data asset registry, retention/policies.ts, stewardship-exemptions.txt). This change is metadata-only: Prisma `///` documentation comments and idempotent COMMENT ON TABLE statements. No physical data shape changes, no rows are created, moved, masked or deleted, and no reader behaviour changes in this slice — the retention sweep still reads policies.ts until slice 4d switches it to pg_catalog. The manifest contract's per-model asset/field resolution is therefore not applicable: every value written here is COPIED from the existing registries by apps/web/scripts/seed-model-metadata-tags.ts (the diff is reviewable one line per model), and the 430 models with no determinable disposition are left untagged in a shrink-only baseline rather than guessed.
compensatingControl: scripts/check-model-metadata-tags.mjs (registered in the source policy guards) fails CI on any tag that violates the closed vocabularies, any purge window on a non-purgeable class, any purge window without a time axis, any retained record without a cited basis, and any NEW persistent model that carries no tag; the untagged baseline can only shrink. The boot-time applier is warn-only (the portal never refuses to start over metadata) and never overwrites a hand-written table comment. packages/db/src/model-metadata.test.ts covers parse/format/catalog round-trips; the applier was dry-run against the development install before merge.
